# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chen_2026_vancomycin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chen_2026_vancomycin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2026.1839423>

Chen 2026 is a machine-learning paper: its deliverable is a CatBoost model that
predicts an individual child's vancomycin clearance (CL) and volume of
distribution (Vd) from six pre-dose variables. The training targets for that
predictor were Bayesian posterior CL and Vd from a population PK model, and
that population PK model is what is packaged here. It is the authors' earlier
paediatric model (Chen 2023, packaged as `Chen_2023_vancomycin`) with the
structure and covariates kept and every parameter re-estimated on the pooled
data of two centres. The CatBoost predictor itself is a tree ensemble with no
published equations and is not representable as an nlmixr2 model.

# Population

The pooled dataset holds 821 critically ill children (suspected or proven
infection plus a pSOFA score of at least 2) treated with intermittent IV
vancomycin for at least 3 days: 753 from Xinhua Hospital, Shanghai (June 2013
to March 2023) and 68 from the People's Hospital of the Inner Mongolia
Autonomous Region (June 2018 to March 2023). They contributed 1767 serum
concentrations, 840 peaks and 927 troughs, measured by HPLC. Children on renal
replacement therapy or ECMO were excluded. Chen 2026 Table 1 reports a median
(IQR) age of 1.75 (0.41-6.41) years, postmenstrual age (PMA) 131.14
(61.43-374.43) weeks, weight 11.00 (6.00-20.00) kg, eGFR 108.40
(85.17-120.00) mL/min/1.73 m^2 and albumin 36.30 (31.60-40.50) g/L; 41.78% were
female, 82.22% were in an ICU and 10.48% were after cardiothoracic surgery
(CTS) on vasoactive agents. Supplementary Table S3 breaks these down by centre.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: one compartment, IV infusion | -- | Methods, 'Population pharmacokinetic (PPK) analysis'; 'Data collection and preprocessing' (1 or 3 h infusions) |
| CL equation | `7.84 * (WT/70)^0.75 * MF * (eGFR/109)^1.02 * 0.783^CTS` | Results, 'Individual pharmacokinetic-parameter estimation'; Supplementary Table S4 notes |
| Vd equation | `36.6 * (WT/70) * (36.2/ALB)^0.255` | Same |
| Maturation function | `MF = 1 / (1 + (PMA/TM50)^Hill)` | Same |
| eGFR equation | `40.7 * (height/SCr)^0.64 * (30/BUN)^0.202` | Methods, 'Data collection and preprocessing'; Table S4 notes |
| eGFR ceiling | 120 mL/min/1.73 m^2 | Chen 2023 framework (Table 2 Model D), retained per Chen 2026 Methods; see Assumptions |
| `lcl` | log(7.84) | Table S4, theta_CL |
| `lvc` | log(36.6) | Table S4, theta_V |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Results equations (constants, no RSE) |
| `pma_tm50` | 37.1 weeks | Table S4, TM50 |
| `pma_hill` | -1.64 | Table S4, Hill |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 1.02 | Table S4, theta_eGFR |
| `e_cts_cl` | 0.783 | Table S4, theta_1 |
| `e_alb_vc` | 0.255 | Table S4, theta_ALB |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 0.283^2, 0.272^2, cov 0.0548 | Table S4, CL (%CV) 28.3, Vd (%CV) 27.2, Cov (CL-Vd) 0.0548 |
| `propSd` | 0.177 | Table S4, Exponential (%CV) 17.7 |
| `addSd` | 0.154 mg/L | Table S4, Additive 0.154 |

# Comparison with the original Chen 2023 estimates

Supplementary Table S4 prints the original and updated estimates side by side.
The packaged models carry exactly those two columns.

```{r param-compare}
fixef_of <- function(name) {
  m <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(name))
  ini <- m$iniDf
  ini <- ini[!is.na(ini$ntheta), ]
  stats::setNames(ini$est, ini$name)
}
p23 <- fixef_of("Chen_2023_vancomycin")
p26 <- fixef_of("Chen_2026_vancomycin")
show <- c(lcl = "theta_CL (L/h)", lvc = "theta_V (L)", pma_tm50 = "TM50 (weeks)",
          pma_hill = "Hill", e_crcl_cl = "theta_eGFR", e_cts_cl = "theta_1 (CTS)",
          e_alb_vc = "theta_ALB", propSd = "Exponential/proportional", addSd = "Additive (mg/L)")
back <- function(p) ifelse(names(p) %in% c("lcl", "lvc"), exp(p), p)
cmp <- data.frame(
  Parameter = unname(show),
  `Chen 2023` = signif(back(p23[names(show)]), 3),
  `Chen 2026` = signif(back(p26[names(show)]), 3),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Reproduces the fixed-effect and residual rows of Supplementary Table S4 of Chen 2026.")
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(back(p26[names(show)])),
                   c(7.84, 36.6, 37.1, -1.64, 1.02, 0.783, 0.255, 0.177, 0.154)))
)
```

# Simulation helpers

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Chen_2026_vancomycin")
mod_tv <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Typical-value solves over many subjects warn that no omega is present, which
# is the intent here; only that warning is muffled.
solve_tv <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
}
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}

# Intermittent 1-h IV infusions every `tau` h, with a dense observation grid
# over the last dosing day.
make_events <- function(cohort, mg_kg_day, tau = 6, days = 5, tinf = 1, obs_by = 0.1) {
  last_day <- (days - 1) * 24
  dose_times <- seq(0, days * 24 - tau, by = tau)
  obs_times <- seq(last_day, days * 24, by = obs_by)
  ev <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
    r <- cohort[i, ]
    amt <- mg_kg_day * r$WT * tau / 24
    d <- data.frame(id = r$id, time = dose_times, amt = amt, evid = 1, rate = amt / tinf)
    o <- data.frame(id = r$id, time = obs_times, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0, rate = NA_real_)
    out <- rbind(d, o)
    out$cmt <- "central"
    out$WT <- r$WT
    out$PAGE <- r$PAGE
    out$CRCL <- r$CRCL
    out$ALB <- r$ALB
    out$SURG_CARD_VASOACTIVE <- r$SURG_CARD_VASOACTIVE
    out$group <- r$group
    out$mg_kg_day <- mg_kg_day
    out[order(out$time, -out$evid), ]
  })
  do.call(rbind, ev)
}
```

# Structural identities

Deterministic checks on the typical-value model, gated tightly.

```{r identities}
one <- function(WT, PAGE, CRCL, ALB, CTS) {
  ch <- data.frame(id = 1L, WT = WT, PAGE = PAGE, CRCL = CRCL, ALB = ALB,
                   SURG_CARD_VASOACTIVE = CTS, group = "x")
  s <- solve_tv(mod_tv, make_events(ch, 40, tau = 24, days = 1, obs_by = 1),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
  c(cl = s$cl[1], vc = s$vc[1], mf = s$maturation_cl[1])
}
ref <- one(70, 1e6, 109, 36.2, 0)
ids <- data.frame(
  Check = c("CL of the reference adult (L/h)",
            "Vd of the reference adult (L)",
            "Maturation at PMA = TM50",
            "CL at eGFR 200 equals CL at eGFR 120 (ceiling)",
            "CTS multiplies CL by theta_1"),
  Simulated = c(ref[["cl"]], ref[["vc"]], one(10, 37.1, 109, 36.2, 0)[["mf"]],
                one(10, 200, 200, 36.2, 0)[["cl"]],
                one(10, 200, 100, 36.2, 1)[["cl"]] / one(10, 200, 100, 36.2, 0)[["cl"]]),
  Expected = c(7.84, 36.6, 0.5, one(10, 200, 120, 36.2, 0)[["cl"]], 0.783)
)
knitr::kable(ids, digits = 5)
stopifnot(all(abs(ids$Simulated - ids$Expected) < 1e-4 * pmax(1, abs(ids$Expected))))
```

# Virtual cohort

Chen 2026 does not publish individual data, so a cohort is reconstructed from
the Table 1 summaries. Postnatal age is drawn from a quantile function that is
log-linear between the Table 1 quartiles (0.41, 1.75 and 6.41 years) and the
assumed extremes of 1 week and 17.9 years, so the median and IQR match, PMA
is postnatal age plus 40 weeks (the gestational-age imputation the authors'
group uses for children over one year, Chen 2023), and weight follows an
approximate median weight-for-age curve with 15% log-normal scatter. Uncapped
eGFR is log-normal around the Xinhua centre median and IQR of Supplementary
Table S3 (109.3, 86.6-140.5), albumin is normal around the Table 1 median
(36.3 g/L, IQR 31.6-40.5) and 10.48% of children are CTS patients.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261113)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261113)
n <- 400
age <- exp(approx(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), log(c(1 / 52, 0.41, 1.75, 6.41, 17.9)),
                  xout = runif(n))$y)
# Approximate median weight-for-age (kg) of boys and girls combined.
wfa <- data.frame(age = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18),
                  wt  = c(3.3, 6.0, 7.6, 9.6, 12.2, 14.3, 16.3, 18.3, 20.5, 25.6,
                          31.9, 39.9, 49.0, 56.0, 60.0))
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n),
  age = age,
  PAGE = 40 + age * 52.18,
  WT = approx(wfa$age, wfa$wt, xout = age)$y * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.15)),
  CRCL = exp(rnorm(n, log(109.3), log(140.5 / 86.6) / (2 * qnorm(0.75)))),
  ALB = pmax(15, rnorm(n, 36.3, (40.5 - 31.6) / (2 * qnorm(0.75)))),
  SURG_CARD_VASOACTIVE = rbinom(n, 1, 0.1048)
)
cohort$group <- cut(cohort$age, c(0, 1, 4, 10, 18),
                    labels = c("<1 year", "1 to <4 years", "4 to <10 years", ">=10 years"),
                    right = FALSE)
cohort$group <- as.character(cohort$group)
summ <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", median(x), quantile(x, 0.25), quantile(x, 0.75))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Covariate = c("Age (years)", "PMA (weeks)", "Weight (kg)", "eGFR, capped at 120", "Albumin (g/L)"),
  `Virtual cohort` = c(summ(cohort$age), summ(cohort$PAGE), summ(cohort$WT),
                       summ(pmin(cohort$CRCL, 120)), summ(cohort$ALB)),
  `Chen 2026 Table 1` = c("1.75 (0.41-6.41)", "131.14 (61.43-374.43)", "11.00 (6.00-20.00)",
                          "108.40 (85.17-120.00)", "36.30 (31.60-40.50)"),
  check.names = FALSE
), caption = "Median (IQR) of the virtual cohort against Chen 2026 Table 1.")
```

# Individual CL and Vd against the Table 1 posterior estimates

Chen 2026 Table 1 reports the distribution of the individual Bayesian
posterior CL and Vd that the updated model produced for the 821 children:
CL 1.56 (0.69-3.01) L/h and Vd 5.80 (3.22-10.82) L. Individual parameters
simulated with between-subject variability over the virtual cohort should
reproduce the centre of these distributions. The tolerance is loose because
the cohort is reconstructed from marginal summaries.

```{r posterior-compare}
ev_one <- make_events(cohort, 60, tau = 6, days = 1, obs_by = 6)
sim_iiv <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_one, returnType = "data.frame",
                           keep = c("group"))
indiv <- sim_iiv |>
  group_by(id) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup()
pk_cmp <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("CL (L/h)", "Vd (L)"),
  Simulated = c(summ(indiv$cl), summ(indiv$vc)),
  `Chen 2026 Table 1` = c("1.56 (0.69-3.01)", "5.80 (3.22-10.82)"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(pk_cmp, caption = "Median (IQR) of individual CL and Vd: simulation against the Table 1 posterior estimates.")
stopifnot(
  abs(log(median(indiv$cl) / 1.56)) < log(1.3),
  abs(log(median(indiv$vc) / 5.80)) < log(1.3)
)
```

```{r cl-weight, fig.cap = "Individual CL and Vd across the virtual cohort against body weight. The dashed lines mark the Chen 2026 Table 1 posterior medians at the Table 1 median weight of 11 kg."}
indiv |>
  select(id, WT, cl, vc) |>
  pivot_longer(c(cl, vc), names_to = "param", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(param = recode(param, cl = "CL (L/h)", vc = "Vd (L)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(WT, value)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(data = data.frame(param = c("CL (L/h)", "Vd (L)"), y = c(1.56, 5.80)),
             aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 11, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~param, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Body weight (kg)", y = NULL)
```

# Updated and original typical clearance across renal function

```{r egfr-curves, fig.cap = "Typical CL of an 11 kg, 131-week-PMA child across eGFR under the original (Chen 2023) and updated (Chen 2026) estimates, with and without CTS. Both flatten above the 120 mL/min/1.73 m^2 ceiling."}
grid <- expand.grid(CRCL = seq(20, 200, by = 5), CTS = c(0, 1))
cl_curve <- function(name) {
  m <- rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(name))
  ch <- data.frame(id = seq_len(nrow(grid)), WT = 11, PAGE = 131.14, CRCL = grid$CRCL,
                   ALB = 36.3, SURG_CARD_VASOACTIVE = grid$CTS, group = "x")
  s <- solve_tv(m, make_events(ch, 40, tau = 24, days = 1, obs_by = 24),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
  s |> group_by(id) |> slice(1) |> ungroup() |>
    transmute(CRCL, CTS = ifelse(SURG_CARD_VASOACTIVE == 1, "CTS", "non-CTS"),
              cl, model = name)
}
curves <- bind_rows(cl_curve("Chen_2023_vancomycin"), cl_curve("Chen_2026_vancomycin"))
ggplot(curves, aes(CRCL, cl, colour = model, linetype = CTS)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 120, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)", y = "Typical CL (L/h)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
```

# AUC-targeted initial dosing with PKNCA

The Chen 2026 Discussion turns a predicted CL into a total daily dose as
`Dose = target AUC24 / CL`, with 400-600 mg*h/L as the MRSA target. For a
one-compartment linear model that identity is exact at steady state, so it
doubles as a check of the packaged model through PKNCA: each virtual child is
given a daily dose of 500 mg*h/L times its own typical-value CL, split every
6 h as 1-h infusions, and the steady-state AUC over day 5 must equal 500.

```{r auc-dosing}
tv <- solve_tv(mod_tv, ev_one, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  group_by(id) |> slice(1) |> ungroup() |> select(id, cl_tv = cl)
dosed <- cohort |>
  left_join(tv, by = "id") |>
  slice_head(n = 120)
ev_auc <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(dosed)), function(i) {
  r <- dosed[i, ]
  make_events(r, mg_kg_day = 500 * r$cl_tv / r$WT, tau = 6, days = 5, obs_by = 0.1)
}) |> bind_rows()
sim_auc <- solve_tv(mod_tv, ev_auc, returnType = "data.frame", keep = c("group"))

conc <- sim_auc |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)
doses <- ev_auc |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, group)
o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | group + id)
o_dose <- PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | group + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 96, end = 120, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals,
                        options = list(auc.method = "linear")))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)
auc <- nca_res |> filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast")
knitr::kable(
  nca_res |>
    group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
    summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("<1 year", "1 to <4 years", "4 to <10 years", ">=10 years"))) |>
    arrange(group) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
    rename("Age group" = group, "AUC24,ss (mg*h/L)" = auclast,
           "Cmax,ss (mg/L)" = cmax, "Cmin,ss (mg/L)" = cmin),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Median steady-state exposure on day 5 for a daily dose of 500 x CL, by age group."
)
stopifnot(all(abs(auc$PPORRES / 500 - 1) < 0.01))
```

Chen 2026 reports no NCA parameters (Cmax, AUC, half-life) of its own, so no
side-by-side comparison against published NCA values is possible; the
day-5 AUC equals the target to within 1% in every child, as the closed form
requires.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **eGFR ceiling retained.** The printed Chen 2026 CL equation and the
  Supplementary Table S4 formula notes show `(eGFR/109)^theta_eGFR` without a
  ceiling. The packaged model keeps the 120 mL/min/1.73 m^2 ceiling of the
  Chen 2023 final model because (i) Chen 2026 states that 'the original
  structural and covariate framework was retained' and only the coefficients
  were re-estimated, and (ii) the Table 1 eGFR summary has its upper quartile
  at exactly 120.00, while the per-centre uncapped summaries of Supplementary
  Table S3 reach 140.5, which is what a ceiling applied in the analysis
  dataset produces. Users should supply the uncapped eGFR.
* **Omega scale.** Table S4 gives the CL and Vd variabilities as %CV and their
  covariance on the omega scale. The diagonals are encoded as
  `(%CV/100)^2`, consistent with the covariance, following
  `Chen_2023_vancomycin` for the same table layout.
* **Residual error.** The combined exponential-plus-additive error is encoded
  as proportional-plus-additive; the exponential arm becomes its first-order
  proportional equivalent because rxode2 cannot solve a log-normal arm combined
  with an additive arm.
* **CTS as a time-varying covariate.** Chen 2026 handled CTS as time-varying in
  the PPK model; the vignette holds it constant per child for simplicity.
* **eGFR units.** Chen 2026 Table 1 and the subgroup tables label eGFR as
  mL/min, while the Methods equation and Supplementary Table S4 notes give
  mL/min/1.73 m^2; the equation is BSA-normalised by construction, so the
  model uses mL/min/1.73 m^2.
* **Virtual cohort.** The cohort is reconstructed from Table 1 and Table S3
  marginal summaries with an approximate median weight-for-age curve; the
  covariate correlations of the real cohort are not available.
* **Not packaged.** The CatBoost CL and Vd predictor, the paper's main
  deliverable, is a tree ensemble and has no closed form.
